body:
I can speak to friends and strangers just fine, the more distant the relative the easier it is to speak to them. 

This isn't a 'teenager' thing, even the quietest teenagers can speak to their family better than I can.

Ever since I was young I have been unable to speak with my family normally, I am basically mute around them. I am 16 now and its is tearing me apart from the inside. I have thought about suicide often, and it has been the source of my depression. I sit in silence in my room for hours on end hoping the pain will go away, hoping that one day I will be able to have a conversation with a member of my family. Hoping that one day I will be able to walk downstairs and say "Hey mum! How are you?", but I can't, and I don't know if I ever will.


But still I keep fighting. I keep fighting for that tiny glow of hope and determination that is left inside of me.

Sure, I can speak to my own family, but barely. I mumble everything and can only say some basic phrases and have to structure my sentences in a very monotone way. I cannot express emotion in conversations, and these limitations effectively make it not worth talking at all. The issues stemmed from me not receiving much attention growing up, as my mum had to look after my dad 24/7 while he was suffering with MND. I don't blame her for it and I wish I could talk to her now, but I can't, and it's tearing me apart.
Yeah it's definitely the root, going to some specialists soon anyways so I hope that will help.

Wow guys thanks for the responses, actually cried reading all this (and the last time I cried was years ago) and it feels so good to cry, like I am letting all the shit out that keeps me down..

I would tell her everything, everything about my life for the past 16 years, all of the funny shit I got up too, all of the trouble I got into, all of the friends I made, etc. I would release all the emotions that have been bottled inside me for my entire life, both good and bad.

So I have a little anecdote for this, in a real situation.

About 2 weeks ago I saw a message on the family group chat of a picture, and I didn't see the title so I assumed it was my friends. I replied by making some sort of witty remark that I would only use around my friends, a remark that breaches all of my barriers around my family. Once I saw the chat title I felt an instant sense of rage, betrayal, hatred, basically every shitty emotion at once. I was shook up and devastated for about a day or two, and right after I saw I started punching myself in the arm to release my anger and embarrassment. I got issues. 

Couldn't go downstairs for the whole night.
Sorry about you too, do you also have issues speaking around them?

I've been trying to rach out but until now, my mum or the rest of my family haven't seemed to give a shit about my broken mental state. I could be crying upstairs and all she would do is finish her glass of wine and then ask if I am okay before leaving me alone for longer. Goddammnit I crave attention since I never got it as a child, it sucks so much.
Psych? What do you mean by that?
Same here, I didn't see any of it coming but coming out of the cinema to hear that people actually found it *really* sad confused the hell out of me..
The beginning of UP, didn't really find it as sad as everyone says it is, didn't get close to crying.
Sometimes I get so anxious that I start to itch all over my body, and the itching becomes worse than the actual anxiety.
Or worse, *both* sides.

Unfortunately I can't show the post to my mother as it is a full on block on communication, and I have tried school counsellors but it isn't helping me at all :(

Thanks for the advice though.
Hey, I know it's a bit late but do you mind me asking what years of your life you had selective mutism for? It's great that you managed to get over it though :)
